title: Frontend Developer
tagline: Build the parts of a web page that people see and use
description: Start with your first web page. Add words with HTML, choose colours with CSS, then make buttons work with JavaScript. Later, try tools that help you build bigger apps. Go at your own speed.
audience: Anyone who is new to code and wants to make a web page

stages.title: HTML foundations
stages.description: Add headings, words, links and pictures to your first page. HTML labels each page part.

stages.title: Styling with CSS
stages.description: Choose colours, sizes and spaces. Learn to arrange page parts on small and large screens.

stages.title: JavaScript
stages.description: Make things happen when someone clicks. Use values, choices and loops to change the page.

stages.title: TypeScript
stages.description: Check whether a value should be a number, some text or another kind. Catch simple mix-ups early.

stages.title: Pick a framework: Angular or React
stages.description: Choose Angular or React to build an app from small page parts. Learn this after the first four steps.

stages.title: Git and GitHub
stages.description: Learn how to save code changes and work with others. Check the topic card to see if its lessons are ready.

stages.title: Portfolio projects
stages.description: Try three projects: a page about your hobby, a quiz with buttons, and a small app with more than one page.
stages.topicNote: This is a practice idea, not a separate lesson. Use the HTML playground for your hobby page. Add CSS colours and JavaScript buttons when you are ready. Save a copy of your code.

seo.title: Frontend Developer Learning Path
seo.description: A step-by-step roadmap from HTML and CSS through JavaScript and TypeScript to Angular or React, Git and portfolio projects.
